title: Kenyan Chocolate Mousse
community: Urban Kenya — the elegant dinner party and restaurant dessert
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Chocolate Mousse — dark chocolate and Kenyan espresso mousse, light and airy from whipped cream and egg whites, rich and complex from the chocolate and coffee. Served in individual glasses with passion fruit coulis.
longDesc: Chocolate mousse is one of those desserts that appears effortless but requires precision — the right chocolate temperature, the right fold, the right refrigeration time. Made with Kenyan espresso-enhanced dark chocolate and topped with passion fruit coulis, it is the complete hotel restaurant dessert experience.
ingredients: 200g dark chocolate (70%) — melted and cooled to 40°C
steps: Melt chocolate with espresso. Cool to 40°C.
Whisk egg yolks into the cooled chocolate.
Whip cream to soft peaks. Fold into chocolate.
Whisk egg whites to stiff peaks with sugar.
Fold egg whites into chocolate mixture in three additions — gently, maintaining volume.
Spoon into glasses. Refrigerate 3 hours minimum.
Make coulis: blend passion fruit pulp with honey. Strain.
Spoon coulis over the set mousse before serving.
chefTips: The chocolate must be at 40°C before adding eggs — too hot scrambles them.
Fold, never stir — stirring deflates the mousse.
Egg whites in three additions maintains maximum volume.
commonMistakes: Chocolate too hot — scrambled eggs in chocolate.
cookingScience: Chocolate mousse is a three-phase foam stabilised by fat (from cream and chocolate). The egg white foam provides the air structure; the cream fat stabilises the air bubbles; the chocolate fat creates a matrix that firms during refrigeration. The espresso provides small amounts of caffeine that slightly inhibit fat crystallisation, keeping the mousse softer.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan espresso in the mousse — local coffee supporting Kenyan farmers.
culturalNote: Chocolate mousse with passion fruit coulis is one of Nairobi's most beloved restaurant desserts — the marriage of dark chocolate intensity and passion fruit's tropical brightness is as natural as Kenyan coffee and milk.
